statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases to 22% as the afternoon give-back stalls: the 30,737.07 cash session low has held since 17:00Z, SMH and NVDA have recovered off marginal new lows, the 10-year has slipped to 5.28% from a 5.30% session high and VIX is down 4.70%.
recommendation: Tail remains inside the watch band at 22%, so the mapped policy state stays WATCH. The downside-aligned configuration flagged at 17:31Z has not extended. Cash NDX is 30,775.52, which is 38.45 points above the 30,737.07 session low that has now survived a full hour, 93.62 below the 30,869.14 opening print and 242.01 points, 0.78%, under the 31,017.53 session high. The three components that were pinned to their lows an hour ago have each come off them: SMH at 630.11 sits 1.56 above a marginal new 628.55 low, NVDA at 234.68 sits 0.49 above a marginal new 234.19 low, and the 10-year at 5.28% is two basis points below a fresh 5.30% session high. VIX at 15.62 is 4.70% lower and in the lower half of its 15.42-16.24 range, and WTI at 91.61 is 1.35% lower after the G7 reserve announcement. That combination is a stalled retracement inside the day's range, not extension away from value, which is why Tail steps back one point rather than up. The published danger window covers 19:00Z to 21:00Z: the Friday power hour, the 20:00Z cash close and the final futures hour into the 21:00Z weekly settlement. Escalation would be a decisive loss of 30,737.07 with the 10-year holding above 5.28%; invalidation would be a reclaim of the 30,869.14 opening print. Stress holds 79% on the unresolved long-end and energy channels.
headline: Cash NDX 30,775.52 holds 38 points above a session low that has now survived an hour, with SMH, NVDA and the 10-year all off their extremes, easing Tail to 22%
body:
NQ December futures trade 31,031.75 (+271.25, +0.88%) on a quote timed 18:16:41Z, inside a 30,760.25-31,282.25 session range from a 30,771.25 open on about 496.2k contracts, with a 31,045.00/31,045.75 bid/ask. The defining development of this hour is a negative one: the extension that the previous hour identified as the live risk did not happen. Cash NDX is 30,775.52 (+273.96, +0.90%) on an 18:26:23Z quote against a 30,869.14 open, and the 30,737.07 session low is unchanged from an hour ago, which means it has now held through a full hour of trading rather than giving way. The index sits 38.45 points above that low, 93.62 below its own opening print and 242.01 points, 0.78%, under the 31,017.53 session high.

The cross-sectional alignment that justified lifting Tail at 17:31Z has partially decayed. SMH is 630.11 (+12.30, +1.99%) at 18:26:39Z against a 628.55-636.25 range: it printed a marginal new low of 628.55 during the hour and has recovered 1.56 points off it, where an hour ago it was trading exactly at its low. NVDA is 234.68 (+3.82, +1.65%) at 18:26:57Z against a 234.19-237.87 range, so it too made a marginal new low and has lifted 0.49 off it, leaving it 3.19 below the 237.87 intraday record it set earlier today. A marginal new low that is immediately bought is the signature of a completed retracement rather than of repeated extension after failed pullbacks.

The long end behaved the same way. The CBOE 10-year yield index is 5.28 (+0.04, +0.80%) at 18:11:55Z against a 5.16-5.30 session range, so the yield pushed to a fresh 5.30% high during the hour and then eased two basis points. Trading Economics carries the cash 10-year at 5.29%, up about 4.6 basis points, and notes the yield exceeded 5.34% earlier this week, its highest since 2002; the Federal Reserve H.15 release for 30 September carries 5.29% for the 10-year, 4.88% for the 2-year and 4.20% for the 3-month. The level remains the single most important restraint in this tape, but a two-basis-point fade from a session high is not the aligned amplifier that a block-band Tail would require.

Volatility and energy both point the other way. VIX is 15.62 (-0.77, -4.70%) at 18:11:31Z against a 15.42-16.24 range and a 16.15 open, so implied volatility is compressing into the Friday close rather than bidding. WTI is 91.61 (-1.26, -1.35%) and Brent is near 102.67, lower after the G7 agreement to release up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel over four months, with a substantial diesel volume inside the first 20 days. That is a relief impulse in the channel that has done the most damage to the macro backdrop, where diesel is still up roughly 70% since late February.

The macro frame is unchanged and remains the reason Stress stays in the high band. September payrolls rose just 29,000 against a consensus near 84,000, the unemployment rate rose to 4.2% from 4.1% and average hourly earnings added 0.1%. October rate-hike odds were cut to 16% from 64% a week earlier. A labour market that is cracking while the 10-year trades near a 2002 high is a genuinely difficult environment, and that is a Stress and Confidence input rather than a Tail input until an observed price path denies mean reversion.

The danger window stays narrow at 19:00Z to 21:00Z. It covers the Friday power hour, the 20:00Z cash close and the single futures-only hour that runs into the 21:00Z weekly settlement, at a record-area level that has already failed once today and with liquidity thinning. Beyond 21:00Z the venue is shut: Nasdaq-100 futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday 4 October, which falls outside this 24-hour horizon, so twenty of the twenty-four forecast slots describe a market with no price path at all.

The assessment above rests entirely on independently fetched primary sources, and the stale context was given no weight in Tail, Stress or Confidence.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours are available, covering the 18:00Z hour on 1 October through the 17:00Z hour today. Tail ran from 20% to 27% across the window. It opened at 20% and held that watch floor for thirteen consecutive hours, through the U.S. afternoon on 1 October and the whole Asian session, then stepped to 21% at 07:00Z, 23% at 08:00Z and 22% at 09:00Z as the European-morning advance gained directional efficiency. It returned to 20% for the 10:00Z and 11:00Z hours, then climbed through the payrolls release to 24% at 12:00Z, 25% at 13:00Z and a window peak of 27% at 14:00Z. Those two hours, 13:00Z and 14:00Z, are the only ones in the window published in the block band, and they were published while NQ held within 0.10% of its session extreme with no meaningful pullback. Tail mapped back to 22% for the 15:00Z and 16:00Z hours once a 0.81% retracement was actually observed, then lifted a single point to 23% at 17:00Z when cash NDX, SMH and NVDA were all pinned at or within a fraction of their session lows with the 10-year at a session high. Stress stayed in the high band throughout, between 74% and 79%, and Confidence held 88-89%. Dominant mode was mixed for nineteen of the twenty-four hours, with trend-up recorded only for the 08:00Z and 09:00Z European-morning hours and the 12:00Z to 14:00Z post-payrolls stretch.
outlookSummary: The forecast opens at 22% for the current 18:00Z hour, matching the stalled retracement, then lifts to 24% for 19:00Z and 20:00Z. That pair is the published danger window: 19:00Z carries the Friday power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, and 20:00Z is the single futures-only hour that runs into the 21:00Z weekly settlement, at a record-area level that has already failed once today with the long end near a 2002 high and liquidity thinning. No slot is published in the block band, because the amplifier stack has decayed rather than aligned over the last hour: the session low held, semiconductor and megacap leadership bought their own marginal new lows, the 10-year faded two basis points from a fresh high, VIX is compressing and oil is falling on the G7 release. The escalation condition on the danger-window hours is a decisive loss of the 30,737.07 cash session low together with the 10-year holding above 5.28%; the invalidation is a reclaim of the 30,869.14 opening print or a settlement inside today's 30,760.25-31,282.25 futures range. From 21:00Z the published curve flattens to a 20% watch floor for the remaining twenty-one slots, because CME equity index futures settle for the week at that boundary and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday 4 October, which is five hours beyond the end of this horizon. A closed market offers no price path in which mean reversion could fail, so the floor is not a projected curve; equally, mapping an unresolved record-area weekly close into the lowest band would understate weekend gap exposure, which is why the floor sits at the bottom of the watch band rather than in green. Confidence decays from 89% to 72% across the horizon to reflect that every slot after 21:00Z is an inference from Friday's verified close rather than a measurement, and Stress eases gently from 79% to 76% because a shut venue cannot deliver a drawdown while the long-end and energy channels stay unresolved.
